120	But at this very point, she says, it then comes to Sarah, who also has
121	a struggle, to grasp, facing reality, or
122	the limitation of physical reality, to grasp that there is
123	a possibility that is beyond comprehension, meaning the appearance of Yitzchak, or the appearance
124	of the shared goal of the two of them.
125	So this requires a nesirah, which is the correction, one could say, of how
126	the patriarchs and matriarchs will have to find their face to face, their
127	shared goal.
128	And each time it will really be a kind of dialogue of finding the shared goal.
129	We know that in the absence of dialogue, all sorts of
130	other options are born that fill in.
131	We know the peak, which is the
132	initial dialogue between Yitzchak and Rivkah, which in fact gives birth to
133	the possibility of Yaakov's birthright, until they actually arrive together
134	at the same goal, and then he is sent through the blessing
135	that is actually planned by Rivkah, but not spoken, but then once again
136	a kind of face to face is created.
137	I think that lech lecha is not only a matter of being heard in the world
138	by everyone.
139	And that same Hebrew family of Avraham
140	and Sarai is able to hear this, and not only to hear it, but to take
141	responsibility for it.
142	To take responsibility for it by making souls.
143	So they actually begin to create a group, one could say, that has,
144	whose course is a course of clarification, a clarification of what
145	faith is, of how we relate to the desire to receive
146	versus the desire to bestow, how we relate
147	to the meaning of the possibility of acting responsibly toward the future,
148	toward what is meant to be born.
149	This is what is meant to come out.
150	So this is truly the first beginning of the correction of Adam and Chava, consciously,
151	which succeeds in hearing the calls, and so I suggest that we at least
152	go along this path,
153	in an attempt to read
154	this year the lech lecha.
